statement: For every prime p, set K=F_p and P(x)=x^(p-1)+x^(-1). For every Laurent polynomial Q in K[x,x^(-1)], define u_n=[x^0](P(x)^n Q(x)) for every integer n>=0. Then the following are equivalent: (i) for every i>=0, l>=1, and N>=0 there exists j>N such that u_(j+k)=u_(i+k) for all integers 0<=k<l; (ii) u_n=0 for every n>=0; (iii) Q=P F(P) for some polynomial F in K[t]. The condition in (iii) is the subspace P K[P], not the full Laurent-ring ideal. This covers all primes, including 2, zero Q, and arbitrary finite positive and negative Laurent exponents. It settles source.md for this specified P, without claiming a classification for other degenerate P or higher prime powers.
contribution: Complete ordinary-recurrence and zero-kernel classification for the fixed example in Kohen's Question 20. The proof combines an explicit polynomial lacunary-series reduction with an elementary translated-finite-sums/digit obstruction, covering cancellations among arbitrary Laurent monomials. The inspected current primary sources give density/uniform-recurrence results but no equivalent fixed-P/all-Q ordinary-recurrence classification. This bounded comparison is not a guarantee of priority, and no separate novelty is claimed for the elementary component lemmas.
